Linking Autocorrelation of Gaussian Random Process to Conditional Probabilities

For a zero-mean Gaussian random process X(t), the probability density function (pdf) of the conditional random variable X(t+τ)|X(t)=y is Gaussian. Its properties can be calculated from the autocorrelation (or power spectral density) of the process, Rxx(τ) (or SX(f)).

The conditional expected value is E(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y) = (Rxx(τ)/Rxx(0)) y and the conditional variance is given by

Var[X(t+τ)|X(t)=y] = Rxx(0)(1 − (Rxx(τ)/Rxx(0))2).

The probability P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L is calculated in Wolfram Language as

Probability[x>L, x~NormalDistribution[(Rxx(τ)/Rxx(0)) y, Sqrt[Rxx(0)(1 − (Rxx(τ)/Rxx(0))2)]]].

The connection between the autocorrelation function and the probability P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L is highlighted here. Three autocorrelation functions are considered: Rxx(τ) = 10sinc(10πτ), 10Λ(τ) and 10e−10|τ|. The autocorrelation function and associated power spectral density are plotted. The correlation time τc for each autocorrelation function is shown, where τc = (∫−∞∞Rxx(τ)dτ)/Rxx(0).

P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L is shown as a function of the threshold L and lag τ. This plot shows that P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L approaches P(X(t+τ)>L) as lag τ increases beyond the correlation time. This behavior is expected since the random variables X(t+τ) and X(t) are approximately uncorrelated and, for multivariate Gaussian random variables, uncorrelated implies statistical independence.

The conditional pdf fx(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y) is plotted and the conditional expected value, conditional variance and P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L shown; P(X(t+τ)|X(t)=y)>L is shown as the shaded area. The conditional pdf and the shaded area change as the lag τ, threshold L and conditional variable y are varied.
